correctness.independent_verification: An unbounded four-parameter classification is reduced by a mathematically justified finite branch bound, not by a guessed coordinate cutoff. Independent enumeration exactly checked all branches and the three tests; source verifier was inspected, with a distinct last-coordinate algebraic solver. The previously published Pascal-column theorem supplies only sufficiency.
correctness.rationale: The precise universe is nondecreasing (a,b,c,d) of nonnegative integers and monic positive f_n=product(n+a_i). Necessity of the three proposed tests follows at (n,k)=(2,1),(3,1),(4,2). For a sorted prefix j<4, R_j=product_{i<=j}(a_i+2)/(a_i+1)<R_4 and a prospective next t bounds every remaining factor by (t+2)/(t+1); integrality forces R_j((t+2)/(t+1))^(4-j)>=floor(R_j)+1. Strict decrease in t yields rigorous termination of the exact exhaustive rational sieve. Independent exact Fraction enumeration reproduced prefix counts 1,5,21,143,1867; 83 f2/f1-integer cases; eight also satisfying f1|f3; final five after the third test, with three exclusions 1440/7,500/3,98/3. Sufficiency is not merely 80 finite checks: each surviving f_n is a termwise product of powers of n and rising factorial columns, whose generalized coefficients are integral by Shapiro’s Pascal-column theorem and product closure. Nonnegative shifts, positivity and monic normalization are essential; no arbitrary quartic claim.

value.rationale: Binomid integrality is a natural established arithmetic property. Classifying all nonnegative integer root-shifted quartics across an unbounded four-parameter family settles a concrete gap after degree-two results, and a three-index recognition criterion is a meaningful finite certificate for an otherwise infinite collection of divisibility conditions. The five positive cases alone would be known examples, but the proved global exclusion supplies the mathematical value.
